collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 17 sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch — that is, states whose form of government is officially a kingdom and whose monarch is exclusively theirs (not shared with other countries via the Commonwealth realm system). For each kingdom the staged row records the Region, Type of Monarchy (Parliamentary / Semi-constitutional / Absolute), Current Monarch, and Year of Accession. The 17 staged kingdoms span 6 regions (Europe 7, Middle East 3, Asia 3, Sub-Saharan Africa 2, North Africa 1, Pacific 1) and 3 monarchy types. The framing 'sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch' was chosen to match common-sense English usage of 'kingdom' — Canada, Australia, Jamaica, and other Commonwealth realms (which share Charles III with the UK but are not constituted as kingdoms themselves) are excluded.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_current_monarchies): universe + filter + value (defines the canonical 43-row current-monarchies wikitable; the 17 staged rows are filtered via the two-clause rule 'Title of Head of State contains King AND not a Commonwealth realm of Charles III'; supplies the per-row Country name and Type of Monarchy cells)
- source_urls[1] (List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states): supporting source for Current Monarch and Year of Accession cells (added in cycle-1 repair). The master 'List of current monarchies' article does NOT have an accession-date column — it has Monarch / Type / Succession / Constitution columns but no Since/Accession field. The per-monarchs article's Since column provides full 'DD Month YYYY (N years, M days)' accession-date strings from which the integer Year of Accession is extracted. The per-monarchs article also supplies the Monarch cell directly, including the Thailand-specific dual regnal-and-personal-name formulation 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' which the master article shows as just 'Rama X'.

Dual-source Tier B instance. Cycle-1 audit identified that the staged Year of Accession cells were not source-grounded by the cycle-0 single-source plan because the master 'List of current monarchies' article doesn't include accession dates. Resolved by adding the per-monarchs supporting article (source_count 1 → 2). Region is curator-derived from standard geographic convention (neither source article includes a Region column; the assignment to Europe/Middle East/Asia/Sub-Saharan Africa/North Africa/Pacific is mechanical and unambiguous for the 17 staged kingdoms).
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (17 sovereign kingdoms with own monarch) is fully source-defined via the cited master Wikipedia article and the explicit two-clause filter rule; partition rule (per kingdom) is source-defined; per-row attribute cells are source-defined via the dual-source plan (master 'List of current monarchies' article for Country and Type; supporting 'List of current monarchs of sovereign states' article for Current Monarch and Year of Accession) and standard geographic convention (Region, curator-derived but mechanical). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical European kingdoms (UK Charles III 2022, Spain Felipe VI 2014, Sweden Carl XVI Gustaf 1973) and major non-European kingdoms (Saudi Arabia Salman 2015, Jordan Abdullah II 1999, Thailand Rama X (Vajiralongkorn) 2016, Cambodia Norodom Sihamoni 2004); harder calibration cells include the smaller kingdoms (Lesotho Letsie III, Eswatini Mswati III, Tonga Tupou VI), recent succession events (Denmark Frederik X January 2024 after Margrethe II's abdication), and the country-renaming/reconstitution edge cases (Bahrain became a Kingdom in 2002, Eswatini renamed from Swaziland in 2018). Row count (17) is comfortably above the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected this from a 7-sub-pick set_filter saturation slate (population > 100M, World Heritage in Danger, rivers > 4000 km, active volcanoes, sovereign monarchies-kingdoms-only, Eight-thousanders, megacities). The user picked the kingdoms angle after a deep-dive on the Filter A vs Filter B ambiguity (Filter A = 31 rows including Commonwealth realms vs Filter B = 17 rows excluding them). The user agreed that Filter B aligns with common-sense English usage of 'kingdom' — Canada/Australia/Jamaica are NOT typically called 'kingdoms' in everyday speech despite having Charles III as head of state.
- Category: set_filter (gap 1; this instance SATURATES set_filter at 5/5 — THIRD CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection and set_operation) primary; geographic (gap 3) secondary because the Region column gives a meaningful geographic axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, set_filter pairs canonically with operation_type=filter; the db_analog 'SELECT ... FROM sovereign_monarchies WHERE constituted_as_kingdom AND has_own_monarch' is the canonical WHERE-predicate filter primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, dual-source (master List of current monarchies + supporting List of current monarchs of sovereign states, latter added in cycle-1 repair to source-ground Year of Accession); gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 2.
- Expected shape: 17 rows × 5 columns; PK = Country.
- Domain: Politics/Government — sixth Politics instance (existing: g20_countries_attributes, eu_member_states_accession_years, eurozone_adoptions_1999_2023, nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals, politically_unstable_countries_per_continent_fsi_alert, fifty_us_states_attributes). The kingdoms instance is a clean form-of-government angle that complements the existing Politics instances (which cover economic unions, defense alliances, state attributes, etc.).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) the 'kingdom' framing required a deep-dive disambiguation with the user — Filter A (any King-titled head of state, includes Commonwealth realms, 31 rows) was rejected in favor of Filter B (constituted-as-kingdom with own monarch, excludes Commonwealth realms, 17 rows) because it aligns with common-sense English usage. The instance's title 'world's reigning kingdoms today — sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch' makes this disambiguation explicit. (b) The Year of Accession cell could shift on any monarch's death/abdication; the snapshot is 2026-05-13 and reflects current monarchs as of that date (Frederik X 2024, Charles III 2022, etc.). (c) Region is curator-derived from standard geographic convention (master article doesn't have a Region column); the 6-value categorical is unambiguous for the 17 staged kingdoms.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets sovereign kingdoms or monarchies.

Why the 'sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch' framing rather than alternatives: a strict 'official long-form name starts with Kingdom of' filter would yield the same 17 rows but read as a legal-document title not a natural question. The 'constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch' framing is more natural English while preserving the unambiguity: it correctly excludes Commonwealth realms (which are constitutional monarchies sharing a monarch, not 'constituted as a kingdom'), principalities (Andorra/Liechtenstein/Monaco — constituted as principalities), sultanates (Brunei/Oman), emirates (Kuwait/Qatar/UAE), grand duchy (Luxembourg), theocracy (Vatican), elective federal monarchy (Malaysia), and Japan's empire-titled monarchy. The Wikipedia per-country article naming corroborates the framing — 'Kingdom of Spain' / 'Kingdom of Saudi Arabia' / 'Kingdom of Sweden' articles exist, but 'Kingdom of Canada' / 'Kingdom of Australia' do NOT exist as Wikipedia articles.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: set_filter pairs canonically with operation_type=filter per references/artifact-contract.md. The two-clause WHERE-predicate (constituted_as_kingdom = TRUE AND has_own_monarch = TRUE) is the canonical set_filter primitive.

Domain selection: Politics/Government — sixth Politics instance; deepens the family but adds a distinct form-of-government angle not covered by existing Politics instances. Alternative classification under Geography (regional kingdoms by area) or Culture (royal history) would be defensible but less canonical. Politics/Government is the operative label.

Post-audit (2026-05-13, cycle 1): the cycle-1 audit raised 1 BLOCKING + 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Year of Accession not grounded by the declared single source: the cycle-0 source_urls listed only the master 'List of current monarchies' article, but that article's table has columns for Title/Monarch/Type/Succession/Constitution and does NOT include an accession-date or 'Since' column. The staged Year of Accession cells were implicitly relying on per-country article infoboxes that weren't in source_urls. Resolved by adding the supporting article 'List of current monarchs of sovereign states' to source_urls (source_count 1 → 2). The per-monarchs supporting article has a 'Since' column with full 'DD Month YYYY' accession dates for all 17 staged rows, from which the integer Year is extracted. (b) HYGIENE — Thailand Current Monarch cell: the master 'List of current monarchies' article displays Thailand's Monarch as 'Rama X' (regnal title only); the per-monarchs supporting article uses the dual form 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' (regnal title + personal name); the cycle-0 staging used 'Vajiralongkorn' (personal name only) which doesn't exactly match either cited source. Resolved by updating the cell to 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' to match the per-monarchs source's verbatim form (now in source_urls). All other 16 monarch-name cells already matched the per-monarchs source's verbatim form (Charles III, Felipe VI, Salman, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, Frederik X, etc.), so Thailand was the lone outlier. Net cycle-1 changes: 1 CSV cell repair (Thailand: 'Vajiralongkorn' → 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn'); 1 new source URL added (source_count 1 → 2); narrative updates in temporal_note, source_coverage_notes, and decision_log Source-plan bullet for the dual-source pattern.

Resolved by sweeping the residual stale phrases: (a) _extraction_notes Source-plan now says 'source_count = 2' with explicit dual-source roles (master article for Country and Type; per-monarchs article for Current Monarch and Year of Accession); _extraction_notes step-(5) pipeline now references the per-monarchs supporting article for Current Monarch and Year of Accession (instead of the prior 'master Monarch column' / 'per-country article infobox' framing); _extraction_notes confidence-gradient row for Thailand now reads 'Rama X (Vajiralongkorn) 2016' instead of 'Vajiralongkorn 2016'. (b) decision_log Pre-gate bullet now references the dual-source plan instead of 'per-country Wikipedia article infoboxes'. (c) normalization_decisions Current Monarch paragraph now states the source-of-truth is the per-monarchs article and documents the Thailand-specific dual form 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' (replacing the prior 'Vajiralongkorn... not Rama X' framing which was inconsistent with the cycle-1 cell update). (d) normalization_decisions Year of Accession paragraph now references the per-monarchs Since column instead of 'per-country Wikipedia article infoboxes'. Net cycle-2 changes: 0 CSV changes; 0 source_urls changes; 4 narrative cleanups across draft.json _extraction_notes and curation.json decision_log + normalization_decisions to align all narrative with the dual-source pattern and the Thailand 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' cell value.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 17 sovereign states constituted as a kingdom with their own monarch, defined by a two-clause filter on the master Wikipedia 'List of current monarchies' Table 1 (43-row main current-monarchies wikitable): (a) Title of Head of State contains 'King' (with the source's verbatim formulations 'King' / 'Dragon King' for Bhutan / 'King Queen Mother' for Eswatini's dual-monarch system all included); (b) the country is NOT a Commonwealth realm of Charles III (excluding the 14 non-UK Commonwealth realms — Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, The Bahamas, Belize, Canada, Grenada, Jamaica, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Solomon Islands, Tuvalu — which share Charles III as head of state but are not themselves constituted as kingdoms). The UK is retained as the original kingdom whose monarchy the Commonwealth realms share. The two-clause filter mechanically yields 17 rows. Country name normalization: the staged Country cell uses the conventional short-form English name (Belgium, Denmark, Netherlands), not the master article's longer 'Kingdom of Denmark' / 'Kingdom of the Netherlands' formulations. The short-form is the conventional everyday-English name and matches the Wikipedia per-country article title for these countries (e.g., the Wikipedia article is titled 'Denmark', with 'Kingdom of Denmark' as the long-form alias). Other countries' short-form names match the master article directly. United Kingdom is the conventional short-form for the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Region normalization: 6-value categorical (Europe, Middle East, North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, Pacific) curator-derived from standard geographic convention. Per-row assignments: Europe (UK, Spain, Belgium, Denmark, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden); Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Bahrain — Bahrain is Arabian Peninsula); North Africa (Morocco); Sub-Saharan Africa (Lesotho, Eswatini); Asia (Thailand, Cambodia, Bhutan); Pacific (Tonga). The Middle East / North Africa boundary follows standard usage (Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco are North Africa; Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states are Middle East; Jordan is Middle East). Morocco vs Middle East: Morocco is conventionally classified North Africa rather than Middle East per geographic-region convention. Type of Monarchy normalization: 3-value categorical (Parliamentary / Semi-constitutional / Absolute) taken verbatim from the master article's Type of monarchy column. Distribution: Parliamentary 10 (Belgium, Cambodia, Denmark, Lesotho, Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Thailand, UK), Semi-constitutional 5 (Bahrain, Bhutan, Jordan, Morocco, Tonga), Absolute 2 (Saudi Arabia, Eswatini). Current Monarch normalization: name taken verbatim from the supporting per-monarchs article ('List of current monarchs of sovereign states') Monarch column. For 16 of 17 rows the per-monarchs column uses a regnal short-form (e.g., 'Frederik X' for Denmark; 'Salman' for Saudi Arabia — without surname or full title; 'Charles III' for UK; 'Felipe VI' for Spain). The Thailand row is the lone exception: the per-monarchs source uses the dual regnal-and-personal-name form 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' (Rama X is the regnal title; Vajiralongkorn is the personal name). The staged Thailand cell preserves this dual form to match the source verbatim. (Note: the master 'List of current monarchies' article uses just 'Rama X' for Thailand without the personal name; the per-monarchs supporting article's fuller 'Rama X, Vajiralongkorn' is preferred because the per-monarchs article is the source-of-truth for the Monarch cell.) Year of Accession normalization: 4-digit integer of the year the monarch assumed the throne, extracted from the supporting per-monarchs article's Since column (which has full 'DD Month YYYY (N years, M days)' accession dates). The year is the YYYY component of the date. Most-recent accessions: Frederik X (Denmark, January 14, 2024 — following Queen Margrethe II's abdication); Charles III (UK, September 8, 2022 — following Queen Elizabeth II's death). Earliest: Carl XVI Gustaf (Sweden, September 15, 1973). Alphabetical sort: the CSV is sorted alphabetically by Country name (Bahrain, Belgium, ..., Tonga, United Kingdom), matching the standard convention for fixed-entity-list instances.
open_questions: 1. Whether to widen the universe to include 'all sovereign monarchies' (43 rows total) rather than the narrower 'kingdoms with own monarch' (17 rows). The current narrow universe was chosen for common-sense alignment; a v2 'sovereign monarchies' variant would cover the broader 43 (including principalities, sultanates, emirates, theocracy, federal elective, empire). 2. Whether the Region categorization should follow UN regional classifications (5 macro-regions) or the curator's 6-region split (Europe, Middle East, North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, Pacific). The current 6-region split is finer-grained for the staged 17 rows; a UN 5-region split would group Middle East and Asia (or split North Africa into Africa). 3. Whether to add a 'Year Kingdom Constituted' column (e.g., Bahrain became a Kingdom in 2002 — was an emirate before; Cambodia restored its monarchy in 1993; Eswatini renamed from Swaziland in 2018). This would add a temporal axis but complicate the schema. 4. Whether the Current Monarch cell should use the regnal name in full ('King Charles III of the United Kingdom') or just the regnal short-form ('Charles III'). The current short-form matches the source's convention. 5. Whether the Type of Monarchy categorical should use Wikipedia's verbatim values (Parliamentary / Semi-constitutional / Absolute) or a more common-sense relabeling (Constitutional / Semi-constitutional / Absolute, replacing 'Parliamentary' with the broader 'Constitutional' which most people would recognize). The current verbatim source labels preserve source-fidelity; a v2 relabeling would prefer common-sense readability. 6. Whether to include Eswatini's dual-monarch system explicitly (the Wikipedia source's Title says 'King Queen Mother' indicating co-monarchs Mswati III and his mother Ntfombi as Ndlovukati). The staged Current Monarch cell uses 'Mswati III' (the male King); a v2 could expand to 'Mswati III; Ntfombi' for dual-monarch transparency.
